items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names describe intent (apiRequestAfterSale, renderStatsAndLogs, showBackupFeedback, remainingPayable), sections are marked with banner comments, and formatting is consistent. Short names like p/v/l only appear as loop variables in render code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: A single new 3045-line index.html caps this at accept. Refund logic is copied: the after-sale preview recomputes `round2((returnedOriginalSum * order.payable) / order.subtotal)` and the last-refund rule in the UI instead of calling a shared function.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Import is validated and failures return {ok:false} without changing data. Stock and quantity guards exist, and all 25 hidden tests passed. But money is floats passed through round2, discount and coupon numbers are magic constants, and some UI inputs use Number(...) loosely.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Has a confirm modal (openConfirmModal, used for reset), status badges, a refund preview box, and toasts. But handleImportFromTextarea and handleFileImport overwrite data with no confirmation, and submitAfterSaleModal records the refund straight away with no confirm step.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls the same api* functions as the test API, stats come from apiGetStats each time, and import is validated before state changes. But money is float arithmetic with round2 rather than integer cents, and the preview duplicates the refund allocation logic.
